"Getting cheaper" = 10% or more below the 1-year median (`cheaper_move`) AND below the multiple exactly one year ago (median across the three; up to a month earlier when the data has a gap). "Getting dearer" = the mirror. Otherwise "Steady"; no direction with under 0.9 clean years. Both tests are needed because a fall back from a spike is not a de-rating: RBC's P/E went 45.5× (Oct 2025) → 70.3× (Jun 2026) → 49.8×, 14% below its 1-year median but 4% above a year ago, so it is Steady. The results table shows the direction as a coloured chip (green "↓ Getting cheaper", grey "→ Steady", red "↑ Getting dearer"; the user asked for colour so the direction reads at a glance) and "vs own level: 1 yr · 3 yr · 5 yr · 10 yr"; the hover text gives each multiple's medians, the year-ago values and the single-day price/EPS split.
- Trend lines (company section): EV/EBITDA change from the close 3, 5 and 10 years ago to today (↓ or ↑ beyond ±10%, → otherwise), split into enterprise value and EBITDA: 1 + multiple change = (1 + EV change) ÷ (1 + EBITDA change). Hover text: the P/E split (price and EPS) and the last 12 months. A horizon that starts before the clean window (a deal plus 12 months, or a listing) is replaced by one "since <month year> (n yr)" line when that is at least 1 year; otherwise "n/a, business changed <month year>". EV/EBITDA is the trend metric because it stays positive through one-off losses (MTU's 2023 GTF charge made trailing P/E negative) and is not moved by interest, tax or acquisition amortization. Do not go back to a 12-month trend: the user found it too short.
- Stale series: P/E rebuilt from filed EPS (`pe_now_override`); EV multiples scaled by enterprise value today ÷ on the last date and flagged.
- Forward P/E (Fiscal.ai forecasts, mostly adjusted EPS) is shown in the company section and changes no light or label. "P/E distorted" when trailing ÷ forward > 1.5. "Earnings expected to fall" (v4.8, `fwd_fall`) when forward P/E is more than 15% above trailing P/E, with the implied forward EPS change (analyst estimates; a flag only). Forward P/E is mostly on adjusted EPS and trailing on GAAP EPS, so a company with large one-off charges or amortization can trip it without a real fall (Bel Fuse: forward EPS −58%). BellRing: 8.2 ÷ 6.7 = 1.23, forward EPS −19%.
- Why not EV/Sales or FCF yield: EV/Sales rises when margins rise (it read Parker-Hannifin's margin gains as "expensive"), and FCF yield jumps with working-capital and capex timing.
- The multiples compare the stock only with its own past. They are not a valuation.

**Result: one action label per company (`result()` in screener.py).** Each label answers "should research time go here now?"; the reason is the first line under it.
- **Research now** (yes): Business green, Management not red, no accounting red flag, not short history, no earnings-falling check fired, and either the median multiple percentile at or below the 50th (`research_now_pe`) or the direction "Getting cheaper" at any level (`cheaper_counts`, the user's option B). For the second route the lines are "Good business, getting cheaper: multiples X% below their 1-year level and Y% below a year ago" and "Still above their usual level (73rd)". Otherwise: "Good business, multiples below their usual level (41st)"; "Research line $210.32; price 2% below it" (+ " — close" when less than 5% below, `near_line_price`).
- **Quick look** (a short, time-boxed check now): an average business — Business yellow, or green with a red Management light (not short history, no red flag), or any Business light green or yellow with exactly one earnings check firing (v4.9; two or more = Not now, v4.10) — and the median percentile at or below the 33rd (`low_in_range_pe`). Lines: "Average business, but multiples low in their own history (29th)"; "Check why it is average on <measures>".
- **Research at lower price** (not yet; research has not started): the same good business as Research now, median percentile above the 50th (or not meaningful) and not getting cheaper. Lines: "Good business, multiples above their usual level (73rd)"; "Research below $434.00 (−14% from today)" (+ " — close" within 5 percentile points, `near_line_pts`). The user rejected "Watchlist" (does it mean watch or research?) and "Wait for price" (it read as research done, waiting to buy).
- **Not now** (no), with the reason first (tested in this order: accounting red flag, too early, weak business, an open Business light, earnings falling now (v4.8; read as an average business since v4.9), average business; user, 23 Oct 2026, so a company whose scores are for information only reads Too early, not Weak; earnings falling now comes before any good or average reading of the record): "Average business, multiples not low in their own history (84th)" plus the average and weak measures; "Too early: only 2 clean years on the current business" plus "Revisit after FY<L + 3 − n> results"; "Weak business: weak on <measures>"; "Earnings falling now: <the checks that fired>" plus "Multiples not low in their own history (<pct>)" and "Check the recent quarters first: the lights describe the record to FY<L>"; "Accounting red flag: <flag>; revisit when resolved". The user rejected "Average business" and "Too early to judge" as labels because they did not say whether to spend time now.
- Further lines where they apply: "Returns X% vs peers Y%: above / below / in line" (B4 median against the peer median over the same years, ±1 point; not on Not now); "Multiples disagree"; re-look signals — a new CEO within 24 months (`new_ceo_months`, from the collector's `ceo_since`) or a deal above 25% of revenue after the latest year-end — shown as "Re-look signal" on Not now and Quick look and as "Note" on the others. Industry is context, not a gate.

**The map: where each company lands (above the results table; the user asked on 2026-10-21 for a quadrant so a long list reads at a glance).** `quad_map()` in make_html.py. Rows are the Business light: Good (green), Average (yellow), Weak (red), with a row **Earnings falling now** between Average and Weak (v4.10, user 2026-10-27, after BellRing sat in the Average row as an average business): every company with at least one earnings check firing that is not a red flag, too early, weak or open, placed by its multiples, in one box titled NOT NOW (a ring dot marks a one-check Quick look at or below the 33rd). Left to right is the median multiple percentile in the stock's own history; the divider between the two halves is the 50th (the stock's usual level), with thin lines at the 33rd and 67th. Each box is titled with its action: Good and cheaper than usual = RESEARCH NOW, Good and dearer = RESEARCH AT LOWER PRICE, Average and cheaper = QUICK LOOK (below the 33rd), Average and dearer = NOT NOW (average, not cheap), the whole Weak row = NOT NOW (weak business). Each company is a dot at its real position with its ticker: a filled blue dot is Research now, a blue ring is Research at lower price or Quick look, a small grey dot is Not now, so a dot whose label differs from its box (getting cheaper, a red Management light) shows. A green ↓ after the ticker = getting cheaper, a red ↑ = getting dearer. A narrow right column holds companies with no meaningful multiple. **Not judged yet (v4.2; the user found the one-line "Not placed" list under the map hard to read and chose this from two prototypes on 2026-10-21):** a fourth band below the Weak row, set apart by a small gap, hatched grey, labelled "Not judged yet" and titled "NOT JUDGED YET — red flag, too early or Business light open · the dot shows where the multiples sit". It holds every company without a Business row: accounting red flags, too-early names (fewer than 3 clean years after a deal) and a Business light still open (a missing measure decides the colour). Each sits at its real multiple percentile on the same axis (or in the no-multiple column), with a second line under the ticker giving the reason: red "red flag: <the flag>" (material weakness, SEC enforcement (AAER), …), grey "too early · revisit FY<year>" (only "too early" in the narrow no-multiple column), or "Business light open". The band is drawn only when at least one name belongs in it, and the key under the map mentions it only then. Hover shows the label, the percentile and the first reason; a click opens the company's section. Labels just left of the 50th, and labels that would run past the right edge, sit to the left of their dot. The user chose this 2 × 2 with the action written in each box, and asked for the 67th-percentile line and the no-meaningful-multiple column; keep all three. Do not go back to a chart that must be decoded, or to text that repeats the results table: the user rejected the v3 quadrant (Business score 1–5 against P/E percentile, no labels), a dot strip with five marker styles (too many codes), a 3 × 5 ticker grid (not intuitive enough) and reason cards under the map (they repeated the results table). **Notes in a box around the ticker (v4.6 and v4.6.1; the user asked on 2026-10-23 to see what an issue is at first glance, then to put the text in a collapsible box so that other tickers never move when many companies are screened at once):** a ticker with any issue gets a box around it, closed by default, showing the ticker, a ▸ and the number of notes. The box colour is the most serious note. Red = accounting red flag ("red flag: material weakness in controls", "red flag: SEC accounting case (AAER)", "red flag: restated accounts (8-K 4.02)", "red flag: auditor qualified the accounts"). Amber = earnings falling now (v4.8; one note per check that fired; since v4.10 the company sits in the Earnings falling now row), a past issue outside the red-flag horizon ("past SEC case (2016–18), not a red flag"; this replaces the v4.3.2 amber highlight) or the financial risk gate ("high debt: net debt 5.6× EBITDA", or "interest cover 1.8×"). Grey = business changing ("big deal after year-end (31% of revenue)"), a CEO in office under 24 months ("new CEO · Jul 2026"; CEOs of 2–5 years stay as the grey tag in the results table only) and multiples that disagree ("multiples disagree: P/E 78th, EV/EBITDA 39th"). The user chose amber over red for the past issue so red keeps meaning a red flag. A click on ▸ opens the notes as a panel over the map (drawn last, so it covers what is under it and moves nothing); a second click closes it; "Show all notes" above the map opens every box; a click on the ticker still opens the company section. Tickers keep their v4.5 positions: label width counts only the ticker, its arrow and the ▸, never the note text. A note near the right edge opens to the left, and the map grows at the bottom when the lowest note needs room. Names in the Not judged yet band keep their one reason line under the ticker (red flag in red, too early with the revisit year, or Business light open), because the band always had room for it; their other notes go in the box and open below that line. With many open notes on a crowded map the panels cover neighbouring tickers, which is why notes start closed. Never let a note move another ticker.

**The score build-up section (display only; `redesign.py`).** The user found the earlier section too dense to read, so each rule is shown once, the panels do not repeat the factor arithmetic, and detail sits behind links; keep it that way. **Industry charts (v4.11, user 2026-10-26: "I want to visualize these two parts using graphs so I can know visually where each company lands").** The Industry panel opens with two ranked bar charts over the group behind the light (`peer_chart()`): I1, each company's 10-year median ROIC including goodwill, and I2, each company's revenue growth per year (median of the first 3 years to median of the last 3, the B3 method, not a first-to-last CAGR). The company's bar is blue; the dark line is the group median (`peers.i1`, `peers.i2`), which sets the score; shaded zones are the measure's light from `peers.cuts` (green = score 4–5, yellow = 3, red = 1–2) and dashed lines the score cut-offs; a bar beyond the scale ends in an arrow with its full value; † marks a company from another tag in a widened group; companies with no value are listed under the chart. A page-level section "Industry: where each company lands in its peer group" sits above the multiples strip (`ind_strip()`, the user's request the same day): one row per run company, grouped by peer group (the group line gives the Industry light, the reason when grey, the I1–I3 scores and the company count); I1 on a fixed scale of −15% to 45%, I2 of −10% to 30%; grey dots = the other group companies, dark tick = group median, blue dot = the company, ring dot = beyond the scale; values on the right. Axis (v4.11.1, user 2026-10-27: "better format the labels so I can track the numbers better on the axis"): labels every 10% with 0% in bold, faint gridlines every 5% through every company row, the light cut-offs on their own line ("yellow 9%", "green 12%"), and the axis repeated under every group heading and at the bottom. Display only.
- Each part of a company section sits in its own panel with a coloured left edge, a light tint and a heading in the same colour: overview grey, accounting red flags slate, Business blue, Industry teal, Management purple, financial risk gate and earnings falling now brown, information and perimeter light grey. No panel is green, yellow or red, because those colours belong to the lights.
- The overview opens with a Result card (the label and up to six of its lines, with "Research line $X; price Y% below it" kept on one line; the long "Detail" text is dropped because the panels repeat it) and a scorecard: tiles grouped by factor under the factor heading, which keeps its light and average ("✓ 3.8", the user asked to keep it). Each tile shows the measure's 1–5 score in a chip coloured by its light, the code, the key number (the last % or × figure before the first → of the arithmetic; M3 shows both columns; R1 shows net debt ÷ EBITDA) and a short name, and links to its row. The two gates have no score, so their chips read Pass or Fail: R1 from the gate, RF from the red-flag check; the E1–E3 tiles (v4.8, under "Earnings falling now") read Pass, Fail or n/a (not run or not counted), with the deciding change as the key number. A not-scored measure shows "–" and n/a. The multiples table and P/E chart stay on the right.
- Each measure row leads with its result line in larger type, then notes, then a bar chart for any year-by-year series of 4 or more years (B1, B3, B4, I3; dashed line = median; values of 10 or more rounded to whole numbers), then the short inputs. Inputs longer than 34 characters, the rule and the sources sit behind "Full inputs", "Rule" and "Sources" links. Each rule is also listed once, in "How each measure is set" at the top of the section. Long input labels are cut at the first bracket, with the full label in a dotted-underline hover. Bold is kept for the result line and the tile numbers only.
- Red-flag rows: ✓ when clean; red ✗ with its "How checked" note open only for the check behind the company's red flag (matched from the flag label: 8-K Item 4.02, material weakness → internal control, SEC AAER, restatement to correct an error, modified audit opinion, accounting regulator finding); amber "!" with "How checked" open for a past issue outside the horizon (an AAER whose misconduct ended more than 5 years ago; the red-flag tile then reads Pass with "Past AAER" in amber); grey "–" for anything else that is not clean, such as no ICFR report yet for a newly public company or an item marked not scored.
- The Industry peer group is stated once, under the panel heading. Information and Perimeter are folded to one line each (auditor changes, CFO departures, share classes; the window sentence, number of automatic flags, deals listed, data repairs); Perimeter opens with a "window cut by a deal" tag when the window is the current perimeter.
- Every panel is collapsible (v4.5; the user asked on 2026-10-23 for Result, Accounting red flags, Business, Industry, Management and Financial risk gate to collapse like Shown for information and Perimeter and data). A click on the panel heading closes or opens it. These six and "Earnings falling now" (v4.8) open by default; a closed panel keeps its header line: the Result label and its first line, the red-flag result, each factor's light and average, for the financial risk gate the gate result with net debt ÷ EBITDA and interest cover, and for earnings falling now the state of E1–E3. A scorecard tile or any in-page link opens the closed panels around its target before scrolling there.
- No number, score, light or label changes in this section.

**Screening records (v4.3; designed with the user on 2026-10-22; vault rule 20; `vault_records.py`).** The user wanted to record why a company was not moved forward and, on later refreshes, to see whether an excluded company may have changed. The record stores the condition that excluded the company and tests on each run whether it still holds, because a screened-out company has no thesis yet; what can change is the reason it was excluded.
- One permanent note per screened company (all labels, not only Not now) in `research/screens/records/`. Frontmatter = latest state (Bases reads only frontmatter); body = a "Latest" block between `<!-- screener:latest:start/end -->` markers, a "Your notes" section, and a "History" table with one row per run, newest first, old rows never rewritten.
- **Two separate reasons.** The screener's reason (`screener_label`, `screen_reason`, `reason_line`) is written by the engine. The user's reason lives in four fields only the user fills: `our_decision` (`move forward` / `not now`; blank = not reviewed), `our_reason`, `our_reopen_if` (something observable) and `our_check_date`. Never fill, infer or reword them.
- **`screen_reason`** (closed list): `good-cheap` (Research now), `average-cheap` (Quick look), `good-not-cheap` (Research at lower price), `average-not-cheap`, `weak-business`, `too-early`, `red-flag`, `earnings-falling` (v4.8; Not now only: a Quick look from earnings falling now is `average-cheap`) (the five Not now reasons), `out-of-scope`. **Reopen tests** on the next run: good-not-cheap → label becomes Research now, multiples getting cheaper, or price at or below the recorded research line; average-not-cheap → the company now counts as a good business (Business green and Management not red; the record's reopen line names the light that made it average: "Management light no longer red while the Business light stays green" for McKesson, "Business light turns green with the Management light not red" otherwise) or median percentile ≤ 33rd (v4.7; before, a green-Business, red-Management name was marked Look again with nothing changed); weak-business → Business no longer red or a red Business measure scores higher; too-early → no longer too early; red-flag → the flag is gone; earnings-falling → no earnings-falling check fires; every reason → a better label, a new re-look signal (new CEO, deal above 25% of revenue; compared by meaning since v4.7.1), or the user's `our_check_date` passed. `reopen_status` (renamed by the user on 2026-10-22 from closed / due / triggered, so each value says what to do): **No action** (nothing has happened), **Check now** (a date has passed: the next annual report should be out, or the user's check date; nothing tested yet), **Look again** (the reason the company was left out no longer holds, or the price reached the research line; never a buy signal). Only a full run sets a status back to No action.
- **No change, no reopen (v4.7).** A reopen condition cannot be met when nothing moved since the record (label, lights, measure scores, median percentile, price, flags, rules version): the status stays No action and the reason says to check the record. The user's own `our_check_date` still sets Look again.
- **Next check** = the date the next annual report should be out: the latest fiscal year-end moved to the next fiscal year, plus 75 days (the revisit year for too-early names; for earnings-falling names the next quarterly report, about 3 months after the run). The fiscal year-end comes from the fact file (`fiscal_year_end_latest`, or the ICFR year-end); without it, one year after the run.
- **Leading indicator** (display only): `b1_latest`/`b1_median` and `b4_latest`/`b4_median`, the latest year against the window median, in the record and in the B1/B4 notes on the page. The lights use 10-year windows and 3-year medians, so a real turn in a business can take 2–3 years to change a light; these two columns show it first. They change no score, light or label.
- **Price at the screen**: `price_at_screen` and `price_date` (the date of the last daily P/E), so the returns of excluded names can later be checked against the names kept. Prices and the research line are in `price_currency`, the currency of the listing the screener priced, with that listing's FocusAlpha symbol in `quote_symbol` (v4.9, 2026-10-27); `currency` is the reporting currency. They differ for Coca-Cola Europacific (EUR reporter, Nasdaq in USD), FEMSA (MXN, NYSE ADR in USD), Canadian National and CPKC (CAD, NYSE in USD) and Coca-Cola HBC (EUR, London in GBP).
- **Weekly price check** (a scheduled task, Mondays 09:35 Asia/Shanghai, bound to the user's computer): for `good-not-cheap` records it compares the FocusAlpha delayed quote of the record's `quote_symbol` (London pence divided by 100) with the recorded `research_line` in `price_currency`, never across listings or currencies (on 26 Oct 2026 it compared Amsterdam €99.90 with Coca-Cola Europacific's $110.24 line and set a false Look again), and sets **Look again**; any No action record whose `next_check` or `our_check_date` has passed is set **Check now**. It writes only `reopen_status`, `reopen_why`, `last_price_check` and `last_price`, and notifies the user. The research line is fixed at the run date (earnings and net debt of that day), so a Look again from price is a reminder; the next full run decides.
- **Screen Register views** (`Screen Register.base` in the vault): 3–7 short columns with set widths and one combined B · I · M lights column, so no view needs side-to-side scrolling (the user's request). An open Base tab in Obsidian can save its older view settings over a change made on disk: ask the user to close the tab before the Base file is rewritten.
- **Backfill** of a run made before v4.3: `vault_records.py snapshot-html <page.html> <out.json> --as-of <run date> [--fy-end <json of {ticker: {date, source}}>]`, then `write --snapshot <out.json>`. The page rounds bar labels to whole percent at 10% or more, so backfilled latest-year values are whole numbers; the record says so in 来源说明.
- The records never touch a decision page's conclusion fields, and a record's label is a research-priority call, not a buy or sell view.

**The results table.**
- Columns: rank, company, Result (label and its lines), Business light, Industry light, Management light with the CEO-change tag under it (colour and symbol only, no numbers; the number is in the hover text and in the company section), multiples in their own history (mini bar of the median percentile, the three percentiles on one line, the direction word, the 1/3/5/10-year comparison), flags (each flag label once). Nothing else: measure lights, peer groups and arithmetic sit in the company sections.
- Order: Research now, Quick look, Research at lower price, Not now; inside each label: average, too early, earnings falling now, weak, red flag; then by median percentile.
- The table stays the full record; the map above it is the quick read.

## Open decisions (apply the current rule and flag the effect)

Numbers are kept so that references stay valid; decision 5 is closed, and decision 10 (the definitions doc) is under Source of truth. The full text of each decision, with the cases behind it, is in `CHANGELOG.md`.

- **D1. Leverage year.** The risk gate uses the latest fiscal year, not the last twelve months, so a company that borrowed after its year-end is caught only at the next annual report.
- **D2. Pay vote.** M2 uses the latest vote only. Option: the lower of the last two votes (Melrose: 34.4% in 2025, 97.0% in 2026).
- **D3. CEO sales from option exercises.** Exercise-and-sell and sell-to-cover trades are not counted in the 30% test. Counted as sales, Woodward's M1 would fall from 3 to 2. Confirm.
- **D4. Amortization add-back with intangibles kept in capital.** B1 mixes two bases; removing the add-back changed no B1 score in 35 test names. Revisit if it starts to matter.
- **D6. Non-US disclosure gaps.** Where per-person holdings or CEO salary are not published (MTU), M1 stays unscored; non-SEC red-flag checks rest on annual reports and regulator searches.
- **D7. Controlled and founder companies.** Option: score M1 on both the controlling holder and the CEO and take the lower. Not tested.
- **D8. Lease-heavy businesses** (restaurants): lease liabilities push ROIC down. Not tested.
- **D9. Trailing GAAP P/E after write-downs and for young companies.** The median of three multiples limits the damage; a P/E history on adjusted EPS is still open.
- **D11. Universe tags are a draft** (proposed by Claude from GICS, descriptions and segment mix); the user corrects them via the CSV.
- **D12. Test thresholds set by Claude:** Quick look at the 33rd percentile, "close" within 5 points or 5% of price, disagreement at 30 points, the 12-month delay after a deal, "getting cheaper" at 10% below the 1-year median. Revisit after a few runs.
- **D13. Trend start dates are single days**, so a start on a one-off day distorts the line (MTU's 3-year start, one week after the GTF charge); the hover shows the split.
- **D14. B3 substitute with a disposal that was never restated.** The written rule names only the profit definition and recurring costs, so such a series is accepted (Crane: B3 = 4, Research now; marking the unrestated years not comparable gives Not now: too early). Confirm.
- **D15. Screening-record timing.** Next check at fiscal year-end + 75 days; the weekly price check uses the research line from the run date, which drifts between runs.
- **D16. Bases date filters untested** in the user's Obsidian: the "Check now" and "Not rescreened in 12 months" views in `Screen Register.base` use `date(x.toString())` and `today() - "365d"`.
- **D17. 8-K Item 4.02 horizon** counts 3 years from the filing date (user: keep for now), while the AAER counts from the misconduct. Option: count from the last restated period. Decide on the first real case.
- **D18. One post-deal year decides.** With one full year after a deal, that year alone sets the post-deal B1/B4 score and usually carries integration costs (WM FY2025). Accepted as cautious.
- **D19. Settlement accruals include amounts not yet settled** (non-participating subdivisions, pending matters); the whole accrual counts as debt. Option: count only amounts with a signed payment schedule.
- **D20. A derived non-current part.** When a company files only the current part and a rounded total (Cardinal Health), non-current = total − current, marked derived; for Cardinal this is precise to about ±$5m (FY2021–FY2023) or ±$50m (FY2024–FY2026).
- **D21. Losses on businesses sold are not added back to NOPAT.** M3 counts them, but B1–B4 treat them as operating costs in the year booked. Option: add them back like impairments.
- **D22. McKesson's currency-translation release.** The $47m German release has no year split and is taken against FY2021; with it M3 is 14.9% → 3, without it 15.3% → 2 (the Management light stays yellow either way). Decide how to treat a release with no year split.
- **D23. A run company's own row keeps its run window** inside its Industry group (its B1 window since v4.8, so a share-count jump the run cleared no longer cuts it), while other group companies are cut only for separations and share jumps (CPKC: 2 years, no I1 value). Option: the group window rule for every company. With v4.8 Dutch Bros, always in the coffee-shop tag, has an I1 value of its own; the tag reached 4 companies with data, so it no longer widens to restaurants, and it is grey as thin.
- **D24. James Hardie's asbestos liability is not counted as debt.** Payments depend on free cash flow, actuarial estimates and a cap, so it is not a fixed schedule ($128.3m current, $880.3m non-current at Mar 2026), though it is debt-like in substance. Louisiana-Pacific's $27m contingency reserves are mostly environmental and not counted. Decide whether such liabilities count.
- **D25. Deals split across two fiscal years** can pass no single year's 25% revenue test (Conagra's Pinnacle Foods, Campbell's Snyder's-Lance); set the window by hand with `perimeter_start`. Option: a second test on deal revenue ÷ prior-year revenue.
- **D26. The first full year after a big deal trips the revenue test** when it starts the window; clear it by hand with `deal_flags_ok`. Option: ignore that flag automatically.
- **D27. Japanese pay and trade data.** Ask for amounts in yen (collectors gave ¥ millions); Japan has no open-market trade reports, so the net-buyer test is not known; with only a group total of directors' pay, use the average per director and say so.
- **D28. Tax receivable agreements** (Dutch Bros, Zevia) are not counted as debt-like. Decide whether they count.
- **D29. v4.8 thresholds set by Claude, accepted by the user for now (2026-10-27):** E1 15% and 3 points, E2 2 cuts or 15% (a cut = midpoint down 2%), E3 price −50% with operating income down less than half as much, the latest-year test −10%, industry now −25% from the 5-year peak in half the group, concentration 50% and 70%, forward P/E 15% above trailing. E1 and E2 have not yet run on aerospace or services companies: review the limits after the first aerospace run with quarterly data, listing every hit.
- **D34. E1 against the peer group (proposed, not tested).** Fire E1 only when the company falls clearly more than its tag's companies in the same quarters (for example by 10 points), so a sector-wide downturn does not send every cyclical name to Not now; it needs quarterly data for the peers (one more Fiscal.ai pull). Test on the first aerospace run before deciding.

## Lessons from the test runs

- Large results: never print them into the conversation — `mcp_call.py` saves them to a file (`fiscal_exec.py` in the Fiscal.ai versions; the rest of this line describes Fiscal.ai data). Daily ratios come newest first. Interest income is often missing, so net interest = interest expense. Early years can lack a balance sheet.
- Fiscal.ai often has no separate amortization of acquired intangibles (it sits inside D&A on the cash flow statement) and its standardized operating cash flow can include discontinued operations. Both change NOPAT, B1, B3, B4 and B2; the data checks in Step 3 and the fact collectors repair them. For Crane, Fiscal.ai's FY2023 and FY2024 operating cash flow (66.1 and 15.0, $m) equals the filed discontinued-operations line, not the company total.
- Fiscal.ai line labels: FEMSA files "Net Cash Generated by Operating Activities from Discontinuing Operations", which the continuing-operations pattern in `pull_main.js` read as continuing until v4.7.1; check the `cfoSrc` line of a non-US filer when `cfoCont` is far below `cfo`.
- Filings: read sec.gov Archives documents (web search finds the URLs; the filing index `https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/<CIK>/<accession-without-dashes>/` lists a filing's documents). If you fetch with curl, SEC asks for a User-Agent; use a generic one and never put an email or personal data in it. Fiscal.ai `filing_pdf` (base64 → `pdftotext`, through `fiscal_exec.py`) reads full annual reports. Proxies are not in Fiscal.ai `company_filings`.
- Privacy: never put the user's email or any personal data in request headers, URLs or User-Agent strings.
- Charts: the company P/E chart clips at max(67th × 1.8, today × 1.1); keep the mini percentile bar on one line; the multiples strip uses one percentile axis for all names, with a circle, square and triangle for P/E, EV/EBIT and EV/EBITDA and a filled dot for the median.
- Fiscal.ai `ratios_list` marks the ratios with daily history (`hasDailyData`): P/E, EV/EBIT, EV/EBITDA, EV/Sales, P/FCF, FCF yield, enterprise value. Its daily series for MTU stop on 29 June 2026 (missing quarters). `company_stock_prices` is split-adjusted, newest first.
- Fiscal.ai's MTU daily series has no data from 29 Sep 2025 to 2 Jan 2026 and stops on 29 Jun 2026; the year-ago lookup accepts a value up to a month earlier.
- Net debt for the research line must come from enterprise value and market value on the same day: a one-day mismatch gave Crane $459m against $748m filed; same-day figures gave $750.5m.
- In a tight multiple range a few percent moves the percentile a lot (Crane: three multiples within ±7% of their medians spread from the 25th to the 70th percentile; on 21 Oct a 1.6% price rise moved its median from the 41st to the 48th); read the research line in price terms.
- Python's `round` rounds half to even (3.25 → 3.2); factor scores use Decimal half-up.
- Each fact collector works in its own `scratch/<TICKER>/` folder, scripts included; shared folders caused files to be overwritten.
- Railroads and Canadian filers (23 Oct 2026): Fiscal.ai had no stock compensation for CN, CPKC, CSX or McKesson, so collectors supplied it from the notes (pass it as `data_overrides` `sbc`). Form 40-F filers (CN) are SEC registrants for ICFR and AAER; their insiders file on SEDI, which no tool reaches, so insider-trade facts rest on secondary summaries; CN's circular could not be read, leaving M1 unscored. CPKC already sets CEO pay in USD.
- Tokyo listings (23 Oct 2026): Fiscal.ai does not cover them; build `raw/` rows from FocusAlpha `get_japan_financials` and the daily multiples from FocusAlpha prices (from Sep 2021, so a 5-year multiples history; add it as an `extra_flags` line), and pass stock compensation from the facts as `data_overrides` `sbc`. A fact collector can miss an announced deal: check every re-look signal of the last record against the fresh facts (AAR's MRO Holdings deal, 28 Sep 2026, was missing and added from the 8-K). Give a CEO share count in the unit of the quoted price (Oatly's ordinary shares ÷ 20 for its ADS; Monster's holding × 2 after its Aug 2026 split).
- Litigation liabilities: FocusAlpha `get_balance_sheets` does not split them out (McKesson's total debt there, $6,526m + $2,088m leases, equals the engine's debt). Fiscal.ai `company_financials_as_reported` (balance sheet) has the filed line ("Long-term litigation liabilities") with source pages; the McKesson 10-K read by WebFetch was cut before Item 8.
- Settlement debt (23 Oct 2026, v4.7): FocusAlpha `get_filing_items` reads McKesson's and Cencora's 10-K notes; it returns "unparseable_document" for Cardinal Health's 10-Ks and sec.gov is blocked, so Cardinal comes from Fiscal.ai `filing_pdf` (base64 → pdftotext). The current part sits inside accrued liabilities and comes from the litigation note (McKesson's FY2021 current part is filed as "$—"); Cardinal files only a rounded total. Check collected settlement figures against the filing: a charge can be reported instead of the balance (Cardinal FY2020: $5,630m charge, $5,560m balance), and a currency-translation release is easy to miss or mistake (McKesson FY2025: the release is $48m in Note 2; the $62m in the segment note is the Corporate slice of the $667m loss, not the release). Fiscal.ai as-reported labels screen a universe for settlement lines in one pass, but miss settlements inside "other liabilities" (Cardinal has no own line).
- A rule change can move peers too: a run company keeps its run window when it sits in a group, so a change to one company's window can move the whole group's Industry light.
- Grainger discloses only total intangible amortization, mostly capitalized software; software amortization is a recurring cost, so it is not added back (`data_overrides` `am` = 0 and a B1 note). Ask collectors whether the amortization figure includes software.
- Proxy ownership tables were cut off again on 23 Oct 2026 (RSG, FAST, SCI, CTAS, FERG, ROL, MCK); FocusAlpha `get_proxy_ownership` returns the beneficial totals (low confidence, no footnote split). M1 then uses the Form 4 direct holding, and the page says which.
- New universes need peers outside the US only when the US set is thin: waste added Séché, Pizzorno and Befesa. Fiscal.ai `companies_list` (1,000 per page, with `subIndustry`) finds every listed company in a GICS sub-industry in one loop.
- Proxy ownership tables are often cut off by every reader (AAR, Woodward, Crane, StandardAero); collectors rebuild holdings from Form 4s (Fiscal.ai `company_insider_transactions`) and show the arithmetic. Woodward's Form 4s include unvested RSUs inside common stock.
- Peers: a window cut on every goodwill jump removed half the peers (Rolls-Royce, HEICO, Parker, ITT); only separations and share jumps cut the window now. Peer ROIC on the ex-goodwill basis gave absurd values (TransDigm 155%, Safran 159%); use the B4 basis. Rolls-Royce shows about 74% because its invested capital is close to zero (negative equity, customer advances); the median absorbs it. Fiscal.ai has Honeywell Aerospace as `NASDAQ_HONA` (one year of data) and no IHI or SIA Engineering.
- BellRing (26 Oct 2026): a business can look good on every long-window measure while its profit is falling now. Its B3 was not scored (the 2022 spin-off share conversion), but that did not matter: total NOPAT grew 15% a year and every end of the range was green. The trouble sat in the FY2026 quarters and guidance, after the latest 10-K. The earnings-falling checks (v4.8) exist for this; read them before the lights.
- Fiscal.ai coverage (27 Oct 2026, from a count of its 11,996-company list): financial statements exist only for US, Canadian, UK and European listings; Japan, Hong Kong, mainland China, Korea, Taiwan, Australia, Singapore, Mexico, Brazil and India have none or almost none. Peer universes are therefore limited to those regions; Asian peers would have to be built by hand from FocusAlpha (`get_japan_financials`, `get_china_financials`, `get_hk_financials`), as for Tokyo run companies.
- Universe review of 27 Oct 2026 (user asked Claude to decide): peers were added only when they fit the tag definition, earn most of their revenue in that business and have 6 or more years of Fiscal.ai data (I2 needs 6). Rejected: Chagee (4 years), Reborn Coffee (loss-making micro-cap), Ralliant and Mirion (4 years), Asker (5 years), DKSH (healthcare about half of sales, no profit split), Boise Cascade (distribution and wood products earn similar profit), Grupa Klepsydra (3 meaningful years). Deathcare and engines were not marked complete: with 3 companies with data their own group cannot form anyway (needs 4). The instruments tag mixes instrument makers and electronic-component makers; splitting it is open.
- Non-SEC red flags: a restatement the company calls a re-presentation or policy change (Melrose's IFRS 15 gross-up) is not an error correction; the brief asks for `is_error_per_company` and the engine counts only `true`.

## Iterating this skill (Codex, FocusAlpha-only version)

The engine files are the same in all three versions (Claude, Codex with Fiscal.ai, Codex FocusAlpha-only). Rules change only in a new version the skill owner approves, in all three at once. When the user approves a rule change: change `RULES` or the code in `SKILL_DIR/scripts/`, `RULES_VERSION` and `ENGINE_VERSION` at the top of `screener.py`, `rules_version` in `references/config_example.json`, the Rules section here and the fact brief in `references/` if a fact changed; write the rule as it now stands, without the old rule or the story of the change. Update `scripts/CHECKSUMS.txt`, the checksums in Step 0 and the README; re-run the last run from its `raw/`, `facts/` and `config.json` and list every company whose light or label moved. History goes to `references/CHANGELOG.md`, with one line in the Versions list below.

## config.json and page_text.json

`config.json` (see `config_example.json` in the engine bundle):
- top level: `title`, `as_of`, `rules_version`, `output` (HTML file name), `universe_dir` (Step 2b), optional `pe_default_from`. `rules_version` may be left out; when present it must equal `RULES_VERSION` in `screener.py`, or `build` stops (v4.7.2). `build` writes `run_meta.json` (engine, rules version, build time); the page subtitle and the vault records take the rules version and the engine from it, never from text typed into the config or `page_text.json`.
- per company (keyed by ticker): `key`, `name`, `group`; optional `trend_ok` (v4.8: `{"recent" | "guidance" | "price": "<reason>"}`, waives one earnings-falling check with the reason), `perimeter_start`, `perimeter_note`, `deal_flags_ok`, `post_deal_from`, `held_for_sale`, `b3_mix`, `growth_start`, `growth_start_why`, `dil_base`, `downturn`, `pe_from`, `pe_from_why`, `pe_now_override`, `measure_gaps`, `data_fixes`, `data_overrides` (`{column: {FY: value}}`), `red_flag_overrides`, `extra_flags`, `measure_notes` (keyed by B1–B4, M1–M3, R1).

`universe.json`: `name`, `status`, `min_peers`, `tags` (`{code: {parent, label, def, complete?, complete_why?}}`; `complete` since v4.9, set only with the user's confirmation), `parents` (`{code: label}`), `companies` (`{key: {t, name, tag, why, gics, channel?, window_from?, window_why?}}`; `channel` since v4.8, Step 2b), `excluded` (`{key: reason}`).

`page_text.json` (all optional): `tab_title`, `title`, `sub`, `lead`, `moves_title`, `moves_intro`, `moves` (list of `{t, v1, why}`), `problems_title`, `problems_intro`, `problems` (list of `{title, what, fix}`), `notes` (ticker → list of sentences), `method_notes`, `pe_note`, `sources`. Leave `sub` out to get the standard subtitle ("N companies · rules version … (engine …) · prices and P/E to …"). `make_html.py` stops when `sub` or `sources` names a rules version or engine different from `run_meta.json` ("rules version X", "engine vX", "engine vX, rules Y"); a reference to an earlier run's rules in other words, such as "rerun of the 22 Oct records (rules 2026-10-21h)", is allowed.

## Files in this skill

- `scripts/screener.py`: `score` (data measures, perimeter flags, data checks) and `build` (all measures, lights, red flags, multiples reading, action labels → `page_data.json`, `universe_page.json`, `run_meta.json` with the engine, rules version and data route). All thresholds in `RULES` at the top, with `RULES_VERSION` and `ENGINE_VERSION`; `build` stops when `config.json` names another rules version, and when most run companies are off Fiscal.ai and `data_route` is not set.
- `scripts/make_html.py`: the HTML page; calls `redesign.py` and stops if it rewrote fewer company sections than the run has. `scripts/redesign.py`: the score build-up layout (needs `beautifulsoup4`).
- `scripts/mcp_call.py`: FocusAlpha calls outside the chat (`--list`, one call, `--batch`), each full result to a file, pages followed.
- `scripts/build_rows_focusalpha.py`, `build_quarters_focusalpha.py`, `build_qbs_focusalpha.py`, `build_prices_focusalpha.py`, `fa_common.py`: FocusAlpha results → the engine's `raw/main_fa.json`, `raw/quarters.json`, `raw/qbs.json` and `scratch/px_<T>.csv`.
- `scripts/rebuild_multiples.py`: daily P/E, EV/EBIT and EV/EBITDA from the prices and the run's own fundamentals, with an audit table.
- `scripts/vault_records.py`: the screening records in the vault (`snapshot`, `snapshot-html`, `read`, `compare`, `write`; never touches the user's fields).
- `scripts/check_engine.py` and `scripts/CHECKSUMS.txt`: the engine guard; run it after Step 0, before `build` and before `make_html.py`.
- `scripts/shot.js`: Playwright screenshots (desktop, strip chart, chosen companies, mobile).
- `references/fact_brief_template.md`: the fact-collector brief (Step 4 adds the FocusAlpha tool paragraph). `references/config_example.json`: example config with `data_route` set. `references/CHANGELOG.md`: version history (not needed to run the screen).
- `references/universe_industrials_materials.json`, `universe_aero_industrials.json`, `universe_beverages.json`, `universe_services_distribution_transport.json`: the coverage universes (Step 2b). `references/debt_like_services_distribution_transport.json`: fixed-schedule settlement liabilities for that universe.
- `agents/openai.yaml`: display name and the FocusAlpha MCP dependency.
